scn-f725bb77.name: Battery-Assisted Peak Shaving (10kWh system)
scn-f725bb77.rationale: This cafe has only 8% peak coincidence (3-9pm), making it an ideal candidate for battery storage. A 10kWh battery charged overnight at off-peak rates ($0.19/kWh) can discharge during the expensive peak window ($0.43/kWh), reducing grid demand by ~65% during 3-9pm. Complementary operational shifts include pre-cooling with HVAC before 3pm, running espresso warming cycles during shoulder periods, and scheduling oven prep work outside peak. The battery captures the full peak-to-off-peak price arbitrage ($0.24/kWh spread), delivering strong ROI even before retailer switching. Switching to Alinta saves an additional $395/year on the shifted profile.

scn-37c2a2ef.name: Battery Peak Shaving + Smart Load Shifting
scn-37c2a2ef.rationale: Brunswick East Cafe operates predominantly during cafe hours (7am-5pm) with 8% peak coincidence. This scenario models a 10kWh battery system that charges overnight at off-peak rates and discharges during 3-9pm peak to flatten the load profile, combined with strategic pre-cooling, fridge defrost scheduling, and preparation load shifts to shoulder periods. The battery reduces grid draw from 0.945-0.999 kW during peak to near-zero for key hours, while operational shifts move refrigeration cycles, HVAC pre-cooling, and food prep equipment out of the 3-9pm window. Alinta Energy's lower TOU rates amplify savings when combined with the flattened load profile, delivering $395+ annual reduction vs current AGL tariff, plus operational savings from demand charge reduction. Battery economics improve with VIC solar feed-in opportunities and potential ARENA/CEFC incentives.

scn-d198d169.name: Battery Storage with Peak Shaving
scn-d198d169.rationale: Brunswick East Cafe has only 8% peak coincidence (3–9pm) but pays a significant premium during those hours ($0.429/kWh peak vs $0.193 off-peak). Installing a 10-15 kWh battery system would store energy during off-peak/overnight periods (midnight–6am at $0.193/kWh) and discharge during the 3–9pm peak window. This scenario models the effect by shifting portions of fridge cooling, HVAC pre-conditioning, oven prep, and espresso machine warm-up loads away from the 3–9pm peak window. The battery would effectively reduce peak-period grid draw by ~50% for controllable base loads (refrigeration, climate control prep) and 25-40% for cooking equipment. Combined with a switch to Alinta Energy's lower TOU rates, total annual savings reach $405–$485 including both operational shift benefits and retailer arbitrage. Payback period for a commercial battery (~$8,000–$12,000 installed) would be 18–24 months, with additional resilience benefits for a cafe dependent on refrigeration.
